## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mountain-climbing game inspired by *Peak*, where the player uses tools to reach the summit.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a standalone HTML canvas experience titled “SUMMIT — The White Spine,” with keyboard and touch controls.
- Designed climbing around jumping, piton launches, grip stamina, checkpoints, and supply caches.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a visual direction and game UI for the mountain ascent in `index.html`.
- Added game mechanics and rendering code in earlier edits, including movement, pitons, stamina, checkpoints, caches, and summit completion.

### Active
- Repair `index.html`: its current contents end immediately after the opening `<script>` tag, so the JavaScript game logic and closing HTML are missing.
- After repair, run the game in-browser and verify gameplay and visuals; prior screenshot checks did not verify the current file.

### Blocked
- The game is currently not playable because `index.html` is incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Restore the JavaScript and closing markup for `index.html`, using the prior implementation described above or rebuilding it.
2. Run the game and check the browser console for runtime errors.
3. Save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then briefly report the controls and any gameplay assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: sole game file; currently incomplete and needs repair.

## Important Context
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The last complete implementation was overwritten by a subsequent write that left only the page markup and an opening `<script>` tag.
